title: A combobox that filters and creates must call text 'unmatched' by the same rule as the list it shows
rule: When one input both filters a list (fuzzy or prefix) and makes a new item on Enter, decide 'no match, so create' from the filtered rows the user sees (rows.length === 0), not from an exact-name check. Text that still shows a row is a filter: Enter acts on the list (applies, picks). Add a test that types part of an existing name, acts on the row (Space/arrow) and presses Enter, and asserts no new item named after the typed text exists.
rationale: E13.4 (#112): the tagging panel created a tag from the filter text whenever no tag had exactly that name, so 'disp' + Space + Enter tagged every selected font 'disp' and dropped the staged toggle.
